ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure there are two upper and lower ports, and the impedance Z looking in from the left-side port is required. The upper branch, from left to right, has a coil labeled j5 Ω and a coil labeled j2 Ω in sequence; the dot mark of the j5 Ω coil is at the right end, and the dot mark of the top j2 Ω coil is at the left end. The right vertical branch has a coil labeled j2 Ω, whose dot mark is near the upper end. The figure also marks two mutual inductances with arcs, both labeled j10 Ω: one between the top j2 Ω coil and the right vertical j2 Ω coil, and the other between the j5 Ω coil and the right vertical j2 Ω coil. Reasoning: According to the method specified in the problem, assume that the input current enters from the upper-left terminal, flows rightward along the top branch through j5 Ω and the top j2 Ω, then flows downward through the right vertical j2 Ω, and finally returns through the bottom wire. The sum of self-impedances is j5 + j2 + j2. The signs of the mutual inductances are judged from the dot marks: in the top j2 Ω coil the current enters the dotted terminal, and in the vertical j2 Ω coil the current also enters the dotted terminal, so this pair of mutual inductance contributes +2(j10). In the j5 Ω coil, the current flows from left to right into its non-dotted terminal, while in the vertical j2 Ω coil the current enters the dotted terminal, so this pair of mutual inductance contributes -2(j10). The two mutual-inductance terms +2(j10) and -2(j10) cancel each other. Therefore Z = j5 + j2 + j2 = j9 Ω.

method.method_draft: Assume the input current flows from the upper left terminal through the top branch to the right, then down the vertical inductor and back along the bottom conductor. Add the self impedances: j5 + j2 + j2. Determine mutual signs from the dots: for the top j2 and vertical j2 coils, the current enters dotted ends on both, so include +2(j10); for the j5 coil and vertical j2 coil, the current enters the undotted end of j5 but the dotted end of the vertical coil, so include -2(j10). Thus the mutual contributions cancel, leaving Z = j5 + j2 + j2 = j9 Ω.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct coupled-inductor series-loop route: it treats the three coils as series elements carrying the same input current and uses dot-convention signs for each mutual pair, showing that the two mutual terms cancel.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the circuit as a single series path from the left input terminals through a top-left inductor labeled j5 Ω, a top inductor labeled j2 Ω, and a right vertical inductor labeled j2 Ω. Note the dot locations: the j5 coil is dotted on its right end, the top j2 coil is dotted on its left end, and the vertical j2 coil is dotted at its upper end. Also read two mutual reactance labels j10 Ω: one coupling the j5 coil with the vertical j2 coil, and one coupling the top j2 coil with the vertical j2 coil.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to identify that the requested quantity is the input impedance Z shown in the figure; no additional numerical data is supplied outside the image.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the coupled-inductor impedance rule for series-connected coils: self-reactances add, and each mutual coupling contributes ±2jM depending on dot convention. If the series current enters dotted terminals of both coupled coils or undotted terminals of both, the mutual term is positive; if it enters a dotted terminal of one and an undotted terminal of the other, the mutual term is negative.
